title: Git Branching
description: Learn how to work with branches in Git for parallel development

steps.title: Understanding Branches
steps.content:
Branches allow parallel development streams in your repository:

- main/master: Primary branch, stable code
- feature branches: New features
- bugfix branches: Fix issues
- release branches: Prepare releases

Key concepts:
- Branch is a pointer to a commit
- HEAD points to current branch
- Branches diverge from a common ancestor

steps.title: Creating Branches
steps.content:
Create branches to work on features or fixes:

- List branches: git branch
- Create branch: git branch <name>
- Create and switch: git checkout -b <name>
- Switch branch: git checkout <name>

Best practices:
- Use descriptive names
- Branch from latest main
- One feature per branch
- Delete old branches

practical_task.description: Create a new branch called 'feature-1' and switch to it. Type the command you used.
expected_results: git branch feature-1 && git checkout feature-1

steps.title: Working on Branches
steps.content:
Each branch can evolve independently:

1. Create/modify files
2. Stage changes: git add
3. Commit changes: git commit
4. Push branch: git push -u origin <branch>

Tracking changes:
- git status: Check branch status
- git log: View branch history
- git diff: Compare changes

practical_task.description: Create a file, add some content, and commit it to your feature branch. Type 'done' when complete.

steps.title: Branch Management
steps.content:
Keep your branches organized:

- List all branches: git branch -a
- Delete branch: git branch -d <name>
- Force delete: git branch -D <name>
- Rename branch: git branch -m <name>

Remote branches:
- Push branch: git push -u origin <name>
- Delete remote: git push origin --delete <name>
- Track remote: git checkout --track origin/<name>

exercises.question: What is the main purpose of branches?
exercises.explanation: Branches allow multiple developers to work on different features simultaneously without interfering with each other.

exercises.question: What command creates and switches to a new branch?
exercises.explanation: git checkout -b <branch-name> creates a new branch and switches to it in one command.

exercises.question: What command lists all branches?
exercises.explanation: git branch shows all local branches, use -a to see remote branches too.

exercises.question: What command deletes a branch?
exercises.explanation: git branch -d <branch-name> deletes a branch that has been fully merged.
